I love you all." Man City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission. The independent commission found that between 2009/10 and 2017/18, Manchester City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m. The club continue to deny the breaches, with chief executive Ferran Soriano calling the process a "Premier League conspiracy theory" in a video message to players and staff . Confirmation of the Ocon's exit came on Wednesday morning after months of speculation over the 30-year-old Frenchman's future with the team. messages.text: How Man City's 'disguised funding scheme' changed the football landscape

metadata.summary: When Sheikh Mansour completed his takeover in September 2008, marking the start of his ownership with the sensational and then-record signing of Robinho from Real Madrid, Manchester City were a club with two top-flight titles in their 114-year history.
metadata.content: Man City Premier League charges: How 'disguised funding scheme' changed the football landscape - Between the Lines | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Man City Premier League charges: How 'disguised funding scheme' changed the football landscape - Between the Lines Man City are found to have artificially inflated their revenues by £830m using "sham" commercial agreements between 2009/10 and 2017/18; Between the Lines explains how the financial breaches facilitated huge transfer spending and changed the football landscape By Nick Wright and Adam Smith Wednesday 30 September 2026 14:27, UK When Sheikh Mansour completed his takeover in September 2008, marking the start of his ownership with the sensational and then-record signing of Robinho from Real Madrid, Manchester City were a club with two top-flight titles in their 114-year history. The last of those titles had come four decades earlier. City had just finished the 2007/08 season in ninth, 32 points behind champions Manchester United, having suffered an 8-1 loss to Middlesbrough in what proved to be Sven-Goran Eriksson's final game in charge. City had been relegated three times in the Premier League era, dropping as low as the third tier only 10 years earlier. The previous 16 Premier League titles had been shared between Manchester United, Chelsea and Arsenal. City were not in the picture.
